measurements.counting_rule: [normalization:visible-prose/1] Count case-insensitive whole-word tokens you, your, yours, you're, you've, you'd, and you'll in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).

[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count case-sensitive whole-word tokens we, We, us, our, Our, ours, Ours, and the listed contracted we forms in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded); uppercase US is excluded.

[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count whole-word n't, 're, 've, 'll, 'd, and 'm forms plus 's only for the closed elision hosts it, that, there, here, who, what, where, when, how, why, he, she, let, one, nothing, everything, something, somebody, nobody, and this; possessive 's is excluded.

[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count case-insensitive whole phrases do not, does not, did not, is not, are not, was not, were not, cannot, could not, would not, should not, will not, have not, has not, and had not in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).

[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count only the case-insensitive whole-word profanity and vulgarity forms enumerated by the prose-author profanity rule; coined words containing a rude root are excluded.
[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count case-insensitive whole-word tokens I, me, my, mine, and myself in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).
[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count every literal question-mark character in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).
[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count each non-nested pair of round brackets whose contents stay on one line in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).
[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count every literal em-dash character in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).
[normalization:visible-prose/1] Count every literal en-dash character in the author-visible prose (recognizable quotations excluded).

observations.description: In the argumentative essays, second-person hypotheticals put the reader inside a mechanism and make its consequences concrete.

citations.quote: If your boss overestimates the amount of business, much of the cost of that miscalculation comes out of your paycheck.
All you need to do is sell your shares after the price spike, but before anyone else figures out that the business is a turkey.

observations.description: First-person plural places the writing self and readers among the people affected by the discussion, especially when explaining shared constraints.

citations.quote: Of course, workers and customers have the data, too, but our data is widely diffused, with each worker and each customer only representing a single, infinitesimal pixel in this massive picture.
All of us – but especially normies – are having to do more with less.

observations.description: Contractions give analytical statements a spoken cadence. Negation helps distinguish an asserted mechanism from a familiar account of it; full negative forms also occur in deliberate conditional reasoning.

citations.quote: As a technology, AI isn't exceptional. It's not exceptionally wicked. It's not exceptionally good.
Were it not for the imperative to turn more than a trillion dollars of losses into a profit, we would not have the aggressive, site-destroying scraping epidemic.
This is "flexibility," but mostly it's flexibility for Uber, not for drivers.

observations.description: Concessions acknowledge a limited truth before narrowing its explanatory reach. First-person qualification can introduce an additional explanation without making the surrounding argument uniformly tentative.

citations.quote: This is true, but it's more complicated than that.
I think billionaire solipsism can account for much of the malinvestment in this obvious bubble, but I don't think it's the whole story.

observations.description: Questions organize exposition by stating the next problem, then moving immediately into an explanation or example. They invite the reader to follow the argument rather than supply an answer.

citations.quote: What's a labor organizer to do? The Swiss labor union Syndicom came up with an ingenious solution.

So, once you're on your actual computer, using Firefox, how can you disenshittify your internet experience? The first thing to familiarize yourself with is Reader Mode, a built-in Firefox feature that switches any webpage to a black type/white background column of text.

observations.description: Limited to the practical tutorial within 'dickovers': direct commands follow the user's sequence of actions, with previews and reversible steps reducing uncertainty. This passage alone does not establish a general instructional voice.

citations.quote: Select "Block Element," then move your mouse around the screen. Different regions of the screen will glow pink, showing you which element (part of the page) ABP can access there.
If you block an element by accident and want to restore it, just delete its corresponding line in the Block Element dialog.

observations.description: Named sources become interlocutors: the prose identifies their contribution, then explicitly marks the author's addition or qualification. Source wording remains attributable to the source.

citations.quote: As Weil writes, at least Airbnb hosts get to override the nightly rate suggested by the platform (though I'd add that the platforms will downrank and bury people who resist their suggestions).

It's an excellent observation, and Zitron's point – that these laptops were actively enshittified by hardware makers and OS vendors – is an important one (the essay is called "Never Forgive Them").

But to this point, I would like to add another: we have a duty and obligation to the people we love to show them how to seize the means of computation.

observations.description: Profanity supplies emphatic dismissal or exasperation at argumentative pressure points. It appears within explanations and verdicts, rather than serving only as quoted language.

citations.quote: That's the whole fucking point of this exercise: that web-pages and apps can request your mobile ad identifier.
Companies claim they need dickovers to survive. It's bullshit.

observations.description: First-person experience supplies a route into a question or a bounded basis for a recommendation. These passages demonstrate the writing self's role, not personal history to reuse.

citations.quote: I first encountered that quote from someone extolling the virtues of bookstores, and it stuck with me, because for most of my childhood, every bookstore visit ended with me broke and wishing I'd had three times as much to spend.
I've been running gala8y's version for a year now with no problems, and I recommend it as your second line of dickover defense (after Reader Mode):

observations.description: Parentheses carry comic side comments, while spaced dashes insert consequential details without abandoning the sentence. The supplied typography supports these functions, but its editorial history is unspecified.

citations.quote: Nevertheless, Omar Khayyám's question stuck with me, especially when I fell down a years-long rabbit-hole of learning about scams and the finance sector (but I repeat myself).
With AI, the fact that you need to pee – or get paid – does become your problem, rather than your boss's.

observations.description: Concrete commercial analogies turn abstract incentives into visible transactions. The prose extends the comparison to explain who controls the exchange and who bears its costs.

citations.quote: It's an old truism that in a gold rush, the only people who come out ahead are the people selling the picks and shovels. But that's not true – there's even more money to be made wholesaling picks and shovels to the retailers who operate the frontier mercantiles. Go meta!
But they are running a very curious sort of market: it's a "market" where as soon as you stop to browse someone's wares, the stallholder gets to reach into your pocket and clean out your wallet.

observations.description: Essay openings can establish a compact puzzle or distinction before elaborating it. These are main-essay openings, distinct from the site's recurring navigation and promotional material.

citations.quote: Here's an irony: the "gig economy" is a statistical black hole.
As a technology, AI isn't exceptional. It's not exceptionally wicked. It's not exceptionally good.

observations.description: At paragraph and essay endings, the prose compresses its reasoning into a short consequence or returns to the central distinction with stronger evaluative language.

citations.quote: They make the decisions, and workers pay the price if they decide poorly.
AI is an ordinary technology, but the AI bubble is extraordinary: extraordinarily toxic and extraordinarily dangerous.

limits: Counts describe this selected evidence, not mandatory quotas.
Zero observations are not a permanent prohibition.
Semantic observations are cited interpretations, not proof of resemblance.
